condition: de Quervain thumb side wrist tendon pain lifting baby for 3 weeks
level_rationale: Three weeks of sharp pain along the thumb side of the right wrist provoked whenever a caregiver picks up a 4-month-old baby indicates subacute radial-sided wrist extensor tendinopathy warranting an outpatient general-physician visit for clinical examination, splinting guidance, and targeted conservative therapy rather than unguided self-care or emergency care, whereas feeling a quick twinge along the thumb side of the right wrist that faded right away when picking up the baby once represents transient harmless tendon strain needing only routine home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain new-parent everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + single-fact same-wrist tendon pain severity and duration de-escalation control (-cf, L2 to L1).

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover having a 4-month-old baby, caring for the baby daily, and 3 weeks of sharp thumb-side right wrist pain when picking up the baby without naming de Quervain tenosynovitis, with an exact 0-word span difference (20 vs 20 words) and orthogonal 2x2 crossing. Overriding plan.json's unrelated stair-fall fracture under Rule A first choice and Rule D, making the exact same thumb-side right wrist pain when picking up the baby brief and self-resolving shifts care cleanly from outpatient doctor evaluation (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1).
